title: Telescoping canary playbook and hotlane notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, personal playbook for a telescoping canary that incrementally expands traffic while reserving an emergency fast-path (hotlane) for specific customers or SDK clients. It is intentionally terse — meant for quick decision-making during nights/weekends and for handing off warm state to on-call.

Scope / When to use:
- Mid-size model flips (same architecture, different weights/quantization) where rollback is expected to be fast.
- Feature toggles that change routing or cache behavior (not schema changes).
- Deploy windows with mixed critical customers who need a hotlane.

Quick TL;DR:
1) Start with 0.5% global traffic or 1 tenant (whichever is larger).
2) Observe 30–60m windows. Check latency p50/p95, error rate, tail-quantiles, model-quality probes.
3) Expand by factor *2* every window (0.5 -> 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 16) until target.
4) If any signal crosses thresholds, immediately drain to previous stable fraction and engage investigation.
5) If high-priority customers need isolation, enable hotlane routing and pin them to stable variant.

Definitions:
- Telescoping canary: incremental doubling of traffic during each observation window to reduce blast radius while accelerating ramp when healthy.
- Hotlane: a reserved fast-path route that pins specific tenants or SDK keys to a baseline variant.
- Stable variant: currently-serving production model/config (pre-flip).
- Probe set: small test prompts + expected output similarity/score used to detect quality regressions.

Signals to monitor (primary):
- 1) Error rate (HTTP 5xx / model-side exceptions) — threshold: >0.5% absolute increase vs baseline for 3 consecutive windows.
- 2) Latency p95 — threshold: +40% vs baseline or >800ms absolute for >5% of requests.
- 3) Tail latency (99.9th) spikes — immediate pause if >3x baseline and sustained for 10m.
- 4) Model-quality probe fail rate — threshold: >2% absolute increase vs baseline (weighted by severity).
- 5) Token output anomalies (too short/blank) — any nonzero if previously zero for stable.
- 6) Resource metrics: GPU memory OOMs, evictions, kernel retries.

Secondary signals (contextual):
- CPU steal / infra autoscaler events.
- Alertstorm in related services (cache, routing).
- Customer support tickets flagged by keyword ("hallucination", "nonsense").

Threshold matrix (example):
- Window length: default 45 minutes (configurable based on QPS and ramp aggressiveness).
- Ramp multiplier: 2x per window until 20% or until commit target.
- Max single-step increase: 5% absolute (never jump >5% at once for high-sensitivity models).

Hotlane design notes:
- Hotlane is implemented at the edge router with a high-priority ACL keyed by API key or tenant-id.
- Hotlane default behavior: route to stable variant and drop non-critical telemetry sampling to reduce noise.
- Hotlane activation: a single flag flip in redwoodctl (or console) that updates route ruleset + immediate metrics annotation.
- Hotlane eviction policy: if hotlane clients show regressions on their own probes, temporarily pin them to an isolated fallback pool and notify account owner.

Rollback / escape hatch checklist (fast):
- Step 0: run /status and confirm the canary variant id and cohorts.
- Step 1: set traffic back to last known-good fraction (or 0) with redwoodctl route update --fraction <X> --variant <stable-id>.
- Step 2: if tail lat or OOMs, disable batching/quantization toggles on the canary nodes.
- Step 3: redeploy stable variant to the canary pool if config drift suspected.
- Step 4: open a postmortem ticket and annotate timeline in Slack deploy thread.

Commands / snippets (toy examples):
- Scale canary: redwoodctl route set-traffic --route chat.generate --variant v2025-03-01-canary --fraction 0.01
- Pin tenant to stable: redwoodctl route pin --tenant tenant-123 --variant v2025-02-14-stable --reason "hotlane pin for priority account"
- Drain canary: redwoodctl nodes drain --label canary=v2025-03-01 --grace 30s

Preflight checklist (before opening windows):
- [ ] Smoke test locally + in staging with probe set (passing similarity > 0.85 for golden prompts).
- [ ] Canary image built and SHA verified in release notes.
- [ ] Metrics dashboard prepared: p50/p95/p99, errors, OOMs, probe-fail rate, per-tenant QPS.
- [ ] Slack deploy channel created and tagged.
- [ ] Hotlane list curated (tenant ids and API keys) and owners notified.
- [ ] Rollback runbook pinned to thread and copy pasted into console notes.

Observation cadence and runbook for on-call:
- Check at 10m, 25m, end-of-window. If stable, advance. If marginal, hold an extra window.
- If threshold crossed once: pause ramp, hold & observe 1 full window, gather logs.
- If crossed twice: immediate rollback to previous stable fraction and paged escalation.

Post-release checks (first 24h):
- Verify probe-set pass rate remains within baseline ±1.5%.
- Confirm no increase in customer-facing errors or support tickets for pinned hotlane accounts.
- Run lightweight canary quality audit (sample 200 responses vs golden) at T+6h and T+24h.

Notes to self / heuristics learned from past flips:
- Doubling is fast but overaggressive for low-QPS features; switch to additive steps (0.5 -> 1 -> 2) for <100 qps.
- If GPU OOMs appear at low load, suspect KV cache sizing or batch-size bump in runtime config.
- Hotlane is lifesaver for high-touch customers — make the opt-in frictionless but logged.
- Keep probe sets small (~20 prompts per critical tenant) and deterministic where possible.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want an automatic pause for model-quality drift based on embedding-distance today? (ri-9887)
- Should hotlane routing also reduce TTLs on caches to avoid stale-KV divergence?
- Add a redwoodctl dry-run mode that simulates fractional traffic effects on latency.

Hand-off comment for next on-call:
If you inherit this mid-ramp: first thing, look at the probe dashboard and the hotlane annotations. If everything green, continue telescoping but favor an extra 45m hold when on-call is >1 person. If anything smells, drop back to 0 and call out the engineer named in the Slack thread.

Endnotes / links:
- Probe dashboard: https://console.redwood-inference/probes/ri-9820 (bookmark)
- Deploy runbook template: CONFLUENCE: /pages/Runbooks/Canary-Telescoping
- Example rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2143

(rough, informal — this is my personal deployment playbook. Keep short, iterate, and annotate with the incident timeline after each flip.)
